notes: Per-night micro-events · three drawn per watch, seeded by
nights_stood, surfaced when the watchman CHECKS that station
inside the window. Windows are unwrapped hours (21..30; 27 = 3
AM). All of it is a watchman's ordinary texture — stiff locks,
weather, animals — because the design rule of this cartridge is
that the game never confirms anything. The one existing
exception (the light, the three sounds) stays the only one.

events.line: the gate chain has been re-hung with the padlock facing OUT. you always hang it facing in. probably you didn't, this once.
something has been at the mess garbage cans. the lids are on. the cans are two feet from where they live. raccoons are strong. that is a fact about raccoons.
the gutter over the mess door drips at exactly the tempo of a man walking. it needs fixing. it has needed fixing since 1981; the log says so.
cabin 1's shutter bangs once as you come up, then not again while you stand there, however long you stand there.
cabin 2 is colder than the walk to it. it was cold in '77 too — 'cold for august' — you've read the entry.
a wasp nest under cabin 4's eave, new since somebody last looked. asleep now. a daytime problem, if there is ever a daytime.
one mooring rope is wet to the cleat. the others are dry. it has not rained.
the oars are racked in pairs, all matched, which is not how anyone leaves oars. somebody tidy was here. the log doesn't say who is tidy.
beach glass at the waterline, one piece, green, worn round. you pocket it or you don't. the water offers no opinion.
the gate lamp has collected its usual congregation of moths. one is the size of a playing card. it is looking at you. moths cannot look. it is looking at you.
the mess radio is off. it is always off. tonight the OFF has a quality to it, like a held breath. you check the plug. unplugged. good. fine.
leaves banked against cabin 3's door — the wind pattern does that, the hollow between the cabins does that. every camp has a door the wind chooses.
frost on the grass between the cabins. in august. a cold pocket, the bay does that, cold air slides downhill. you write physics in your head the whole walk.
someone has touched up the boathouse trim. recent — you can smell it. the paint matches, which means someone kept the can, which means someone plans to come back.
a car slows on the road past the gate, holds a moment, and moves on. taillights the whole way to the county bend. people get lost. people get lost, at 2 AM, here.
heron prints along the wet sand, in a straight line, evenly spaced, right at the waterline. herons walk like that. they do. they walk like that.
a letter wedged under cabin 2's step, soaked illegible, stamp from a year you can't make out. you file it in the mess lost-and-found box, which is empty, which stays empty.
the smell of cocoa in the mess at 3 AM. the kitchen is locked, and cold. some smells are just memory doing its rounds too.
